metadata.case_name: LAU KOON LOI v. WONG WAI SING AND ANOTHER

plaintiff.occupation_after: security guard (casual/part-time) employed by SA Security

source: The plaintiff was then taken to the Accident and Emergency Department (“A&E Dept.”) Princess Margaret Hospital (“PMH”) where he was diagnosed to have suffered head injuries and some mild swelling on over his right leg.
Dr Leung diagnosed the plaintiff as suffering from neck sprain resulting in brachial plexus injury.
Dr Yuen opined that the plaintiff had suffered a whiplash injury and noted that the plaintiff expressed thinking that he could not go back to his pre-accident job.
The real injury to plaintiff is a whiplash injury to his neck and which has resulted in some disability in the form of pain to his neck and shoulders.
injuries.icd_description: Acute whiplash associated disorder with complaint of neck pain with neurological signs

source: Dr Leung diagnosed the plaintiff as suffering from neck sprain resulting in brachial plexus injury.

To Dr Leung, the plaintiff complained of neck stiffness with tenderness of the left trapezius and sternomastoid muscle upon tilting to the left, tenderness along the lower cervical spine, pain and numbness and reduced grip power in the left hand.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of multiple nerves at shoulder or upper arm level

injuries.description: C5/6 disc protrusion (cervical disc herniation) causing slight narrowing of the spinal canal and slight indentation on the anterior surface of the cervical cord
source: That MRI findings showed : (i) A disc protrusion at only the C5/6 level. It was a postero-central protrusion measuring about 3 mm which caused a slight narrowing of the spinal canal and a slight compression of the anterior aspect of the cervical cord at C5/6 level;

Dr Tsoi further opined that the protruded C5/6 disc could be related to the accident given that the plaintiff had no pre-existing neck problem and that could explain the plaintiff’s symptoms of persistent neck pain since the accident.

I find on the opinion of Dr Tsoi and for the reason given by Dr Tsoi that the protruded disc at C5/6 level was caused by a combination of the degenerative changes to the cervical spine but which was aggravated by the soft tissue muscle sprain when the accident happened. I further accept the opinion of Dr Tsoi that the protruded disc at C5/6 level was the reason for the persistent neck and shoulder pain of the plaintiff.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injuries to the neck

source: From that MRI study, it was seen that there was disc protrusion at C5/6 level causing slight narrowing of the spinal canal and slight indentation on the anterior surface of the cervical cord. Degenerative changes were also identified at C5/6 junction endplates.
That MRI findings showed : (ii) some degenerative marrow signal changes at the C5/6 end-plates; and (iii) no other abnormality.

manifestations.description: continuous neck pain radiating to the right shoulder and to the right forearm
neck stiffness with tenderness of the left trapezius and sternomastoid muscle
pain and numbness and reduced grip power in the left hand
limited range of motion of the neck in all directions
headache and dizziness (post-concussional headache and dizziness)
episodic daily mild neck pain, occurring morning and night, radiating to right shoulder (of mild intensity)
loss of normal cervical lordosis (radiological finding)

adjustment disorder with symptoms of depressed mood, worries about physical symptoms, problems at work, financial difficulty, relationship problems with family members, pessimistic ideas, sexual problems, suicidal idea and sleep problem
reliance on painkillers occasionally for neck pain
inability or reduced ability to turn the head

treatments_received: consultation with panel doctor Dr Yan
physiotherapy (12 sessions at Pok Oi Hospital)
treatments_future: 10 sessions of psychological treatment by a clinical psychologist (recommended)

losses.category: Loss of sexual function and sexual life
losses.description: the plaintiff started to experience problems of erectile dysfunction which had caused him further stress in his relationship with his wife.
adjustment disorder with ... relationship problems with family members

the plaintiff enjoyed his driving work, in particular with heavy vehicles, and which was the only work that he really knew how to do well; he was less fit to resume his pre-accident job and was not reinstated as a tractor driver
